text:
elaine-support: Heads up — Customer 'FinLedger' on Dedicated reporting gaps in Trace View. They say several request IDs show up in the request logs but don't link to any trace, and spans that do show up have misaligned timestamps (start > end for some child spans). Screenshot attached by customer shows empty span list for request 0a1b2c3d.

miya-cs: Reproduced locally with their sample payload. Request ID `0a1b2c3d` returns a trace id in the API response but the trace panel shows no spans. They're on v2.14 of our SDK and using dedicated region eu-west-2.

sam-eng-runtime: @miya-cs can you paste the exact request headers/response (redact PII)? suspect correlation headers are being stripped by the edge router.

miya-cs: Sure — snippet from their debug:

```
Request headers:
  x-redwood-request-id: 0a1b2c3d
  x-redwood-trace-id: 7f9e1c4b
  x-redwood-parent-id: 00000000

Response: 200 OK
Body: {"request_id":"0a1b2c3d","trace_id":"7f9e1c4b"}
```

jamal-eng-infra: Not seeing the trace in ES ingestion at that timestamp window. There are a bunch of partial spans for that trace id in raw-logs but some span ids look truncated — like `9f2a...` instead of 16 bytes.

oliver-sre: :eyes: Could be a UTF-8/byte-length normalization bug introduced in the router protobuf -> JSON conversion last week. Deploy bot shows a config change 3 days ago:

```
deploy-bot: rolled config edge-proxy:fix-trace-headers v2026-03-09
```

sam-eng-runtime: If headers were mangled the trace id in the request logs could differ from the one the runtime uses to aggregate spans. Two things to check:
1) whether parent_id/header values are being truncated in the header parsing code path
2) whether timestamp precision (ns vs us) got changed and caused some children to appear to start after end

elaine-support: Customer reports it started after they upgraded to SDK v2.14 but it might just be coincidental timing with our router config. They've paused traffic for the time being but want a root cause.

jamal-eng-infra: Quick repro steps I used:
- curl to their app with `x-redwood-request-id` set
- tail the raw-ingest logs on ingest-prod for ~5m
- query ES for `trace_id:7f9e1c4b` and `request_id:0a1b2c3d`

I found entries where `parent_id` was missing entirely on spans from the gpu-runtime pod 3/11 14:02 UTC.

sam-eng-runtime: Assigning to runtime oncall @oliver-sre — can you grab the relevant gpu-runtime pod logs? I'll instrument extra logging for incoming trace headers.

oliver-sre: I pulled logs. Saw this error sequence:
```
runtime: invalid span id length: 6
runtime: fallback to generated span id
```
That explains the truncation. Looking at the container env we have `MAX_HEADER_BYTES=512` which was reduced in the proxy change. The header truncation is happening at the proxy and then runtime is generating fallback span ids -> link loss.

sam-eng-runtime: OK that's the likely root cause. Proposed fix: increase `MAX_HEADER_BYTES` back to 8192 on edge-proxy and add a defensive check in header parser to reject truncated trace headers with a 400 so we don't generate orphan spans.

miya-cs: Customer requested ETA. Any ETA for a config rollback or hotfix?

jamal-eng-infra: I can roll the proxy config back in eu-west-2 immediately (5-10m). Will also kick off a runtime patch for header validation (patch -> canary -> prod ~3 hours).

elaine-support: Please post the rollback link and note for customer. I'll update the ticket and include repro steps + mitigation (they can pin SDK to 2.13 as short-term workaround).

sam-eng-runtime: Action items:
- jamal: rollback edge-proxy MAX_HEADER_BYTES in eu-west-2 (in progress)
- oliver: add header validation to runtime and prepare canary
- miya: confirm with customer after rollback if traces restore

deploy-bot: rollback started: edge-proxy config eu-west-2 by jamal-eng-infra

miya-cs: Thanks — I'll wait 10m and re-run the curl test.

elaine-support: Thanks team. Closing loop once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
